infrastructure_note: The AgentV bootstrap repair (commit 2aedf3bae011718e6439f9a51f4cabf394962528) unblocked the harness itself -- both arms now produce a complete gates.json/scoreboard.json verdict instead of harness_failure/missing_scoreboard. But every one of the 3 smoke records still hit the decode timeout: compiler_ms_mean ~23.1-23.2s/record vs. an 8s-configured (24s combined) chunk budget, even though ~51.7s of eval wall was actually granted this cycle.

harness_signal.root_cause: screening_decode_timeout_seconds=8 needlessly under-used the granted eval wall: _fit_screening_decode_timeout_seconds's own wall-fit ceiling for the nominal 70s arm share is (70-20-8)/3=14.0s, but fitted=min(configured=8, 14)=8 -- the configured value, not the wall, was the binding constraint (clamp_bound=0.0 in thrash_timing.json).
harness_signal.repair_summary: Raise screening_decode_timeout_seconds 8 -> 12 (policy.v1.json v4 -> v5), staying under the 14.0s wall-fit ceiling and inside the pre-existing test_climb_policy_measurement_helpers [1.0, 12.0] range. Partial mitigation only: 12s/record is still short of the observed ~23.1s/record cost on this host, so a full-completion replay is not expected; documented as a bounded, evidence-based improvement, not a claimed fix of the underlying host-capacity gap.

next_priorities.hypothesis: Replay the frozen control/canvas arm once more under the raised 12s budget; if still incomplete, the remaining gap (~23s observed vs 12s granted) is a genuine host CPU-throughput/fixture-cost mismatch that needs either a smaller screening_smoke_n, fewer training steps to free more eval wall, or is simply out of reach for wf_smoke_v2 on a CPU-only sandbox within MAX_RUN_MINUTES=3 -- not further blind timeout increases.
